title: R' Gurion
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.33b.4): “R' Gurion — and some say Rav Yosef bar Shemayah — said: When there are righteous people in the generation, the righteous are seized for the generation.”[^1]

In [Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.5.19), folio 13b: R' Yonah went up to R' Guryan; he came out to him wearing a sandal (he was in mourning, and it was Shabbat). R' Yonah said to him: “What do you think — that we learn practice from you? We do not learn practice from a small person.” In [Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.2.2.7) and [Nazir, beginning of chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nazir.8.1.2): R' Guryan in the name of R' Yose bar Chanina. In [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin, chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.5.6.6) [halakhah supplied as ה״V], he spoke in the name of Resh Lakish; and in [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.3.1.4): “R' Gurion said: The Mundelai asked Resh Lakish.”[^2][^3]

In [Jerusalem Talmud Peah 3:7:16 (Hyman cites 3:9)](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.3.7.16): R' Guryan’s sister wrote her property over to her brother; her elder brother went and appeased her — the case came before R' Imi. Hyman suggests that perhaps his brother is R' Menachem, who is mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 9:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Metzia.9.8.2).[^4]

notes.text: The linked Shabbat gives Rabbi Gurion and Rav Yosef beRabbi Shemayah as alternate attributions. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=849&lang=en) also gives the alternative and cites several of the Yerushalmi episodes.

Maaser Sheni and Nazir give Gurion speaking in Rabbi Yose ben Chanina’s name. The linked Gittin gives Gurion in Resh Lakish’s name. Hyman’s printed locator is 5:5, while the supplied transcription has ה״V and the consulted passage is 5:6.

The linked Moed Katan reads Gurion and uses “sandals” in the plural. Hyman gives Guryan and folio 13b; the consulted edition displays 16a. The description “small person” concerns whose conduct may serve as a precedent. In Megillah the people of Magdala ask Resh Lakish, where Hyman gives Mundelai.

The Peah account continues with a second conveyance. The linked Bava Metzia explicitly calls Rabbi Menachem the brother of Rabbi Gurion. Hyman suggests that Menachem may be the brother in the Peah episode.
